qty.note: one 1 lb package, regular fat for flavor

qty.unit: tbsp grated (peel it with a spoon, grate on the fine side)

steps.text: Start the rice so it is ready when the topping is.

Set a nonstick skillet over medium-high, add the pork, and break it into small crumbles with the spatula. Cook 6 minutes until the crumbles sizzle in their own fat; ground pork is safe at 160°F (71°C).

safety.source: USDA FSIS safe minimum internal temperature table

steps.text: Stir in the grated ginger and cook 30 seconds - it should smell sharp and sweet, not raw.
Add the soy sauce, mirin, and sugar; simmer 2 minutes, shaking the pan, until the liquid is mostly absorbed and the pan sizzles again.
Spoon the pork into a bowl and wipe the skillet with a paper towel.
Beat the eggs with a fork. Pour them into the skillet over medium-low and stir slowly into small soft curds for 2 minutes; they are safe at 160°F (71°C).

safety.source: USDA FSIS safe minimum internal temperature table

steps.text: Drizzle the sesame oil over the eggs and fold once.
Fill four bowls with hot rice. Arrange the pork on one side and the egg on the other - soboro-don keeps the two apart so each keeps its own color.
Scatter the green onions and sesame seeds over everything and eat immediately, mixing as you go.

nutrition_per_serving.basis: USDA FoodData Central values committed in apps/ios/Resources/usda_ingredient_catalog.sqlite (matched fdc_id per ingredient in tables/nutrition-map.json), plus the app's shipped core-ingredient table (data.json) for items without an fdc_id; scaled by evidenced gram quantities
